title: hello-managed — a multi-tenant gateway daemon (target: managed)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Two tenants, HS256-JWT auth, per-tenant budgets, hash-chained audit logs.”
beats.script: Two tenants, HS256-JWT auth, per-tenant budgets, hash-chained audit logs. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens README.md now. This is the source or generated artifact behind the current step; focus on the details the first chunk called out.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to answer a run.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to answer a run. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and the shape — a long-running gateway daemon.”
beats.script: Two lines: what it's called, and the shape — a long-running gateway daemon. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 1 through 2 of crewhaus.yaml, rebuilding live slash crewhaus.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Add the agent block
beats.cue: “One agent serves every tenant — and it answers tersely, by instruction.”
beats.script: One agent serves every tenant — and it answers tersely, by instruction. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 3 through 6 of crewhaus.yaml become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Declare tenant-a and its budget
beats.cue: “A tenant is an id plus a token budget the gateway enforces on every call.”
beats.script: A tenant is an id plus a token budget the gateway enforces on every call. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 7 through 11 of crewhaus.yaml become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Declare tenant-b
beats.cue: “Second tenant: same agent, its own budget, its own storage tree.”
beats.script: Second tenant: same agent, its own budget, its own storage tree. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 12 through 15 of crewhaus.yaml become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Only this next block is appended, so the specification grows in the same order the runtime will parse it.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”
beats.script: Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tenants array survives lowering — ids and budgets, exactly as written.”
beats.script: The tenants array survives lowering — ids and budgets, exactly as written. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Prints the IR for target managed — 36 lines, tenants included.

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed — 36 lines, tenants included

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the daemon: GREEN, no key.”
beats.script: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the daemon: GREEN, no key. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot ok (daemon stayed alive for the liveness window).

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (7 anchors); install ok; boot ok (daemon stayed alive for the liveness window)

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget gate, audit chain — one file you own.”
beats.script: JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget gate, audit chain — one file you own. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash daemon.ts now. The relevant implementation is now visible, so the claim can be inspected directly instead of taken on faith.

beats.label: Pin the JWT secret
beats.cue: “Set it ahead of time — at least 16 chars — to pin the secret across restarts.”
beats.script: Set it ahead of time — at least 16 chars — to pin the secret across restarts. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Without this the daemon generates a one-shot dev secret and prints it.

verify.note: without this the daemon generates a one-shot dev secret and prints it

beats.label: Put tenant storage under live/
beats.cue: CREWHAUS_TENANTS_ROOT — line 21 of the daemon we just opened. Keeps the audit log on camera.
beats.script: CREWHAUS_TENANTS_ROOT — line 21 of the daemon we just opened. Keeps the audit log on camera. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. Default is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants; rebasing keeps the take self-contained.

verify.note: default is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants; rebasing keeps the take self-contained

beats.label: Boot the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it.
beats.script: “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. Boots with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials.

verify.note: boots with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-a
beats.cue: The tenant_id claim IS the tenant — HS256 over the secret we just pinned, no key involved.
beats.script: The tenant_id claim IS the tenant — HS256 over the secret we just pinned, no key involved. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Keyless — signing is local HS256 over the secret run-secret exported into this same terminal; proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the checked bundle.
beats.command: TENANT_A_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-a" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless — signing is local HS256 over the secret run-secret exported into this same terminal; proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the checked bundle

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-a
beats.cue: [needs-key] One authenticated call — the client names the session, and runs.create comes back with a runId and the reply.
beats.script: One authenticated call — the client names the session, and runs.create comes back with a runId and the reply. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. Crewhaus.v1 envelope. Measured with credentials: result.runId=run_…, reply “Paris is the capital of France.”
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_A_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"1","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of France?","sessionId":"sess_0123456789abcdef"}}'

verify.note: crewhaus.v1 envelope. Measured with credentials: result.runId=run_…, reply “Paris is the capital of France.”. sessionId is passed explicitly because CLI 0.4.0's managed codegen mints a base36 default id that session-store rejects (expects sess_<16 hex>) — omit it and the gateway answers internal_error. Keyless it answers internal_error too: no Anthropic credentials.

groups.title: One more thing · the invariant target: managed exists to enforce

beats.label: Read tenant-a's audit log
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Hash-chains the audit log so tampering is detectable.” GENESIS → hash → hash → hash.
beats.script: “Hash-chains the audit log so tampering is detectable.” GENESIS → hash → hash → hash. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. Written by the run-create beat. Measured: three records — gateway_request (prevHash GENESIS), policy_decision, model_call — each chained to the previous record's hash.

verify.note: written by the run-create beat. Measured: three records — gateway_request (prevHash GENESIS), policy_decision, model_call — each chained to the previous record's hash

beats.label: Mint a token for tenant-b
beats.cue: Same secret, same daemon — a different tenant_id, and again no key.
beats.script: Same secret, same daemon — a different tenant_id, and again no key. [[pause:1.5s]] This is an offline proof and should complete successfully. Keyless, like run-mint; second tenant declared in the spec's tenants: block.
beats.command: TENANT_B_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-b" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: keyless, like run-mint; second tenant declared in the spec's tenants: block

beats.label: Start a run as tenant-b
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same endpoint, second tenant — the daemon rebases its storage on the claim.
beats.script: Same endpoint, second tenant — the daemon rebases its storage on the claim. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. Creates live/tenants/tenant-b/ on first authenticated call. Measured: reply “Tokyo is the capital of Japan.” sessionId explicit for the same 0.4.0 reason as run-create.
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_B_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"2","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of Japan?","sessionId":"sess_fedcba9876543210"}}'

verify.note: creates live/tenants/tenant-b/ on first authenticated call. Measured: reply “Tokyo is the capital of Japan.”. sessionId explicit for the same 0.4.0 reason as run-create

beats.label: Show the two tenant trees
beats.cue: [needs-key] Two roots. “Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.”
beats.script: Two roots. “Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.” [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay. Measured after both runs: tenant-a and tenant-b, each with its own audit/, sessions/ and state/ subtree.

verify.note: measured after both runs: tenant-a and tenant-b, each with its own audit/, sessions/ and state/ subtree

beats.label: Stop the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon.
beats.script: Take's over — kill the backgrounded daemon. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. Job %1 is the daemon the run-boot beat backgrounded into this same terminal; skip this and the take leaves a process holding :3000.

verify.note: job %1 is the daemon the run-boot beat backgrounded into this same terminal; skip this and the take leaves a process holding :3000
